_comment: Carbon price scenarios in EUR per tonne CO2e. Read at runtime; never hardcode (KARBON_ATLASI.md section 7). CBAM certificate prices update quarterly, so this file is expected to change often — that is the point of keeping it out of R source.

meta.comment: No exchange rate is applied anywhere in this project. Exposure is reported in EUR because CBAM certificates are denominated in EUR. Converting to TRY would import currency risk into a figure that does not carry it, and would make the number unstable for reasons unrelated to carbon.

observed.description: Actual published CBAM certificate prices. The Commission calculates each quarterly price as the weighted average of EU ETS auction clearing prices, published in the first calendar week after the quarter ends.
observed.annual_comment: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Only two of four 2026 quarters are published, so no annual figure exists yet. Averaging the two available quarters into an annual price would be a fabrication (section 8.1). Populate `annual` only once all four quarters are published, and record the aggregation rule used.

low.source_title: Potential Effects of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism on the Turkish Economy
low.source_authors: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) with the Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change / İklim Değişikliği Başkanlığı
low.source_note: Located 2026-09-06. The figure is confirmed in the Ministry's own announcement of the completed study: assuming a CBAM fee of EUR 75/tCO2e on Scope 1 and 2 emissions embedded in goods exported to the EU, potential annual CBAM costs to Turkish industry reach EUR 138 million in 2027. The announcement is the commissioning body's, not the report itself; the report PDF was not located and should replace this URL if it is published.
low.divergence_from_source: THE STUDY USES THIS PRICE FOR A SPECIFIC YEAR, THIS PROJECT USES IT FLAT. The study pairs EUR 75 with 2027 and EUR 150 with 2032, i.e. as two points on a rising path. Here both are applied unchanged from 2026 to 2034, which is a different construct: a flat sensitivity band rather than a trajectory. That is a defensible choice for a what-if control but it is NOT what the source did, and METHODOLOGY must say so rather than cite the study as though it endorsed a flat price.

high.source_title: Potential Effects of the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism on the Turkish Economy
high.source_authors: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) with the Ministry of Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change / İklim Değişikliği Başkanlığı
high.source_note: Same study as `low`. The announcement states that if the CBAM fee rises to EUR 150/tCO2e, estimated costs reach EUR 2.5 billion per year by 2032.
high.divergence_from_source: Same divergence as `low`: the study attaches EUR 150 to 2032, this project applies it flat across 2026-2034.

custom.description: User-defined price set through the UI slider. Carries no source because it is the user's own assumption; the interface must label it as such and must not let it be mistaken for an observed or legislated value.
